title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Cognitive Complexity in LLMs via Linear Probing using Bloom's Taxonomy
abstract: arXiv:2602.17229v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The black-box nature of Large Language Models necessitates novel evaluation frameworks that transcend surface-level performance metrics. This study investigates the internal neural representations of the levels of complexity using Bloom's Taxonomy as a hierarchical lens. By analyzing high-dimensional activation vectors from different LLMs, we probe whether different Bloom levels, ranging from basic recall (Remember) to abstract synthesis (Create), are linearly separable within the model's residual streams. Our results demonstrate that linear classifiers achieve high accuracy across all Bloom levels, providing evidence that level information is encoded in a linearly accessible subspace of the model's representations. These findings provide evidence that the model organizes representations according to Bloom categories early in the forward pass, with representations becoming increasingly separable across layers.

translated_title: 基于布鲁姆分类学线性探测的大语言模型认知复杂度的机制可解释性研究
translated_abstract: 大语言模型的黑箱特性要求我们采用超越表面性能指标的新型评估框架。本研究以布鲁姆分类学作为分层视角，考察复杂度层级的内部神经表征。通过分析不同大语言模型的高维激活向量，我们探测从基础回忆到抽象综合等不同的布鲁姆层级是否在模型的残差流中是线性可分的。我们的结果表明，线性分类器在所有布鲁姆层级上都能达到较高的准确率，证明层级信息被编码在模型表征的一个线性可访问子空间中。这些发现表明，模型在前向传播的早期阶段就按照布鲁姆类别组织表征，且各层之间的表征可分性逐渐增强。
tldr: 本研究利用布鲁姆分类学与线性探测技术揭示，大语言模型在内部表征中以线性可分的方式编码认知复杂度层级，且这种结构在前向传播早期即已形成并随层数加深愈发清晰。
en_tdlr: This study uses linear probing with Bloom's Taxonomy to show that LLMs encode cognitive complexity levels in a linearly separable manner within their internal representations, with this structure emerging early in the forward pass and becoming increasingly separable across layers.
